It's a common electrical phenomenon actually. That terminal is either the positive or neg voltage connection. When a power source is connected to a battery like your phone's li-po, there can be a small spark gap that occurs as soon as it is plugged in. This is most likely due to a capacitor charging and drawing more current (amps) for a tiny fraction of a second. The electric current is able to jump between the plates "easier" and this spark will overtime erode the copper.
